concepts.title: Why Elections Matter in a Democracy
concepts.definition: Elections are essential to a democratic system because they convert the people's will into a government: citizens choose their representatives, reward or punish performance, and keep power changing hands peacefully.
concepts.key_idea: Elections are democracy's heartbeat: votes decide who rules and how long.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest107.txt opening sections (why elections are essential)
question_patterns: why are elections essential to a democratic system
how do elections make the government accountable
what would happen if elections stopped being held - explain
how do voters reward or punish a government
compare elections with other ways of choosing rulers
explain the phrase elections are the voice of the people

solution_steps.explain: Elections let citizens pick between candidates and parties.
Fear of losing the next election disciplines rulers.
Regular elections transfer power without violence.

concepts.title: The Election Machinery: Commission and Process
concepts.definition: An independent Election Commission supervises elections: preparing voter rolls, announcing schedules, enforcing the model code of conduct, overseeing campaigning, polling and counting - so that the whole process stays free, fair and uniform across the country.
concepts.key_idea: A referee above the players: the Election Commission keeps the contest fair.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest107.txt sections on the election commission and process
question_patterns: what are the functions of the Election Commission
describe the steps of the election process from notification to counting
what is the model code of conduct - why is it needed
how are voter lists prepared and updated
why must the commission be independent of the government
explain polling day procedures at a booth

solution_steps.explain: Rolls list every eligible citizen aged eighteen and above.
Schedules and the code of conduct frame fair campaigning.
Secret ballots and transparent counting declare the verdict.

concepts.title: Challenges and the Citizen's Role
concepts.definition: Elections face challenges of money power, muscle power, fake promises and uneven turnout; a vigilant citizen answers by voting without inducement, questioning candidates, checking information and participating beyond election day.
concepts.key_idea: A vote is a trust: informed, un bribed voting is the citizen's duty to democracy.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest107.txt sections on challenges and citizen participation
question_patterns: what challenges do elections face in India - discuss
how does money power affect election fairness
why should voters not sell their votes - explain
how can voters evaluate candidates before voting
what duties do citizens have beyond casting a vote
suggest reforms to make elections fairer

solution_steps.explain: Money, muscle and misinformation bend the voter's will.
Information, scrutiny and dialogue strengthen choices.
Participation between elections keeps representatives honest.
